title: Critics ask: ‘Who is Nepal’s Prime Minister — Balen Shah or Rabi Lamichhane?’ - Khabarhub
description: Critics ask: ‘Who is Nepal’s Prime Minister — Balen Shah or Rabi Lamichhane?’  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Questions are mounting over the government’s handling of the communal unrest in Sunsari’s Dewanganj after Prime Minister Balen Shah and Home Minister Sudan Gurung faced criticism for what many political leaders, analysts, and members of civil society describe as an inadequate public response.

The criticism comes in the wake of Sunday night’s violent incident in Dewanganj-3, Kaptanganj, which has heightened concerns over the country’s security situation and the government’s crisis management.

Amid growing criticism of the government, Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chair Rabi Lamichhane has drawn praise for taking a more visible role in political outreach. Some observers have even begun asking, “Who is Nepal’s Prime Minister—Balen Shah or Rabi Lamichhane?” arguing that Lamichhane has appeared to be taking on responsibilities traditionally associated with the head of government.

Before assuming office, Shah was known for frequently criticizing previous governments through social media and public platforms. Critics now argue that, following the Sunsari unrest, he has limited his public response to a Facebook post issued late Tuesday, without delivering a detailed public address.

As protests, arson, vandalism, and communal tensions spread across parts of Sunsari after the Dewanganj incident, Shah has not made a comprehensive public statement. Home Minister Sudhan Gurung has also been criticized for focusing primarily on deploying security forces rather than taking broader political initiatives to defuse the crisis.

The Home Ministry, however, has said that security agencies have been instructed to conduct investigations and legal proceedings, while district authorities have been directed to take necessary measures to maintain law and order.

Against the backdrop of growing concerns over religious and social harmony in Nepal’s multiethnic and multireligious society, calls have intensified for stronger leadership from the country’s executive branch.

On Wednesday, Lamichhane convened an all-party meeting to discuss the situation. Prime Minister Shah and Home Minister Gurung did not attend the meeting, prompting renewed questions from political observers about the government’s visibility during the crisis.

Following the meeting, Lamichhane met President Ram Chandra Paudel at Shital Niwas to brief him on the meeting’s conclusions and the evolving political situation. Commentators noted that such briefings are typically conducted by the Prime Minister, fueling further debate over the government’s leadership during the crisis.

Several political analysts and journalists have publicly questioned the Prime Minister’s response.

Political analyst Indra Adhikari said the Sunsari unrest was fundamentally a matter of public security and governance rather than economics, arguing that the Prime Minister, Home Minister, and other senior leaders should have attended the all-party meeting and coordinated directly with all stakeholders.

Journalist and author Sudheer Sharma also argued that many responsibilities expected of the Prime Minister—including issuing appeals for calm, convening political dialogue, coordinating with opposition parties, releasing joint statements, urging restraint, and briefing the President—had instead been undertaken by Lamichhane. While he said there was nothing wrong with Lamichhane’s involvement, Sharma argued that the Prime Minister should have demonstrated stronger leadership during such an extraordinary situation.

Senior journalist Kishore Shrestha described the all-party meeting as a positive initiative but maintained that matters concerning peace, security, and communal harmony should primarily be led by the Prime Minister and the Home Minister. He said their absence from the meeting sent an unfavorable message.

Journalist Poonam Paudel argued that the Prime Minister’s official position should be communicated through formal government channels rather than solely through a Facebook post, calling for an official statement from the Prime Minister’s Office.

Journalist Bimal Pokharel said the issue extends beyond whether the Prime Minister and Home Minister attended the meeting, describing it instead as a broader question of leadership during times of national crisis.

Former CPN-UML lawmaker Thakur Gaire also criticized the absence of the Prime Minister and Home Minister from the all-party meeting, saying it projected a lack of urgency and sensitivity toward the crisis unfolding in Sunsari.

The government’s handling of the Dewanganj unrest has continued to attract criticism from political commentators, with many arguing that all political parties and state institutions should work together to restore peace and preserve social harmony. Government officials, meanwhile, maintain that state agencies remain actively engaged in maintaining security, investigating the incident, and preventing further escalation.

काठमांडू : सुनसरी केरऽ देवांगंज म॑ प्रधानमंत्री बालेन शाह आरू गृहमंत्री सूडान गुरुंग क॑ आलोचना के सामना करला के बाद सरकार केरऽ सांप्रदायिक अशांति क॑ निपटै प॑ सवाल उठी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा क॑ बहुत राजनीतिक नेता, विश्लेषक आरू नागरिक समाज केरऽ सदस्य अपर्याप्त जनप्रतिक्रिया के रूप म॑ बतैलकै ।

ई आलोचना रविवार रात कप्तानगंज केरऽ देवांगंज-३ म॑ घटित हिंसक घटना के बाद करलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ देश केरऽ सुरक्षा स्थिति आरू सरकार केरऽ संकट प्रबंधन प॑ चिंता बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

सरकार केरऽ बढ़तऽ आलोचना के बीच राष्ट्रीय स्वतंत्र पार्टी केरऽ अध्यक्ष रबी लामिछाने न॑ राजनीतिक आउटरीच म॑ अधिक दृश्यमान भूमिका निभाबै के प्रशंसा करलकै । किछु पर्यवेक्षक एतेक तक पूछय लगलाह अछि जे “नेपालक प्रधानमंत्री के छथि—बलेन शाह वा रबी लामिछाने?” तर्क दैत जे लामिछाने परंपरागत रूप स सरकार क मुखिया स जुड़ल जिम्मेदारी लैत देखा रहल अछि।

पदभार ग्रहण करय सं पहिने शाह सोशल मीडिया आओर पब्लिक प्लेटफॉर्म के माध्यम सं बेर-बेर पिछला सरकार के आलोचना करय लेल जानल जाइत छलाह. आब आलोचकऽ के तर्क छै कि सुनसरी अशांति के बाद हुनी मंगलवार देर रात जारी फेसबुक पोस्ट प॑ अपनऽ सार्वजनिक प्रतिक्रिया सीमित करी देल॑ छै, बिना कोनो विस्तृत सार्वजनिक संबोधन के ।

देवांगंज घटना के बाद सुनसरी के कुछ हिस्सा में विरोध, आगजनी, तोड़फोड़, आरू सांप्रदायिक तनाव फैललऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, शाह न॑ कोनो व्यापक सार्वजनिक बयान नै देल॑ छै । गृहमंत्री सुधन गुरुंग केरऽ आलोचना भी करलऽ गेलऽ छै कि हुनी मुख्य रूप स॑ संकट क॑ शांत करै लेली व्यापक राजनीतिक पहल करै के बजाय सुरक्षा बलऽ के तैनाती प॑ ध्यान केंद्रित करी रहलऽ छै ।

गृह मंत्रालय, हालांकि सुरक्षा एजेंसी कए जांच आ कानूनी कार्यवाही करबाक निर्देश देल गेल अछि, जखन कि जिला अधिकारी कए कानून व्यवस्था कए कायम रखबाक लेल आवश्यक उपाय करबाक निर्देश देल गेल अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ बहुजातीय आरू बहुधार्मिक समाज म॑ धार्मिक आरू सामाजिक सौहार्द केरऽ बढ़तऽ चिंता के पृष्ठभूमि म॑ देश केरऽ कार्यपालिका स॑ मजबूत नेतृत्व केरऽ आह्वान तेज होय गेलऽ छै ।

बुधदिन लामिछाने सर्वदलीय बैसार बजा कए स्थिति पर चर्चा केलथि। प्रधानमंत्री शाह आरू गृहमंत्री गुरुंग बैठक म॑ नै ऐला के बाद राजनीतिक पर्यवेक्षकऽ स॑ संकट के दौरान सरकार केरऽ दृश्यता के बारे म॑ नया सवाल उठैलऽ गेलै ।

बैठक के बाद लामिछाने शीतल निवास में राष्ट्रपति रामचंद्र पौडेल स॑ भेंट करी क॑ बैठक केरऽ निष्कर्ष आरू विकसित होय रहलऽ राजनीतिक स्थिति के बारे म॑ जानकारी देलकै । टिप्पणीकारऽ न॑ नोट करलकै कि ऐसनऽ ब्रिफिंग आम तौर प॑ प्रधानमंत्री द्वारा करलऽ जाय छै, जेकरा स॑ संकट के दौरान सरकार केरऽ नेतृत्व प॑ आरू बहस बढ़ी जाय छै ।

प्रधानमंत्री केरऽ प्रतिक्रिया प॑ कईएक राजनीतिक विश्लेषक आरू पत्रकार सार्वजनिक रूप स॑ सवाल उठैलकै ।

राजनीतिक विश्लेषक इन्द्र अधिकारी नँ कहलकै कि सुनसरी अशांति मौलिक रूप सँ अर्थशास्त्र के बजाय जन सुरक्षा आरू शासन के मामला छेकै आरू कहलकै कि प्रधानमंत्री, गृहमंत्री, आरू अन्य वरिष्ठ नेता सिनी क सर्वदलीय बैठक मँ शामिल होना चाहिय्यौ आरू सब सरोकारवाला के साथ सीधा समन्वय करना चाहिय्यौ छेलै ।

पत्रकार आरू लेखक सुधीर शर्मा न॑ ई भी तर्क देलकै कि प्रधानमंत्री स॑ अपेक्षित बहुत सारा जिम्मेदारी-जै म॑ शांति के अपील जारी करना, राजनीतिक संवाद बुलाबै, विपक्षी दलऽ के साथ समन्वय करना, संयुक्त बयान जारी करना, संयम के आग्रह करना, आरू राष्ट्रपति क॑ जानकारी देना शामिल छै- एकरऽ बदला म॑ लामिछाने न॑ संभाली लेल॑ छै । हुनकऽ कहना छेलै कि लामिछाने केरऽ शामिल होय म॑ कोय गलती नै छै, लेकिन शर्मा केरऽ तर्क छेलै कि प्रधानमंत्री क॑ ऐसनऽ असाधारण स्थिति के दौरान मजबूत नेतृत्व के प्रदर्शन करना चाहियऽ छेलै ।

वरिष्ठ पत्रकार किशोर श्रेष्ठ न॑ सर्वदलीय बैठक क॑ सकारात्मक पहल बतैलकै लेकिन शांति, सुरक्षा, आरू साम्प्रदायिक सौहार्द स॑ जुड़लऽ मामला म॑ मुख्य रूप स॑ प्रधानमंत्री आरू गृहमंत्री के नेतृत्व होना चाहियऽ । ओ कहलनि जे, बैसार मे हुनकर अनुपस्थिति प्रतिकूल संदेश दैत अछि।

पत्रकार पूनम पौडेल के तर्क छेलै कि प्रधानमंत्री के आधिकारिक स्थिति के जानकारी केवल फेसबुक पोस्ट के माध्यम स॑ नै बल्कि औपचारिक सरकारी चैनल के माध्यम स॑ करलऽ जाय, जेकरा म॑ प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय स॑ आधिकारिक बयान के आह्वान करलऽ गेलै ।

पत्रकार बिमल पोखरेल नँ कहलकै कि ई मुद्दा प्रधानमंत्री आरू गृहमंत्री बैठक मँ भाग लेलकै कि नै, एकरा सँ आगू बढ़ी क एकरा बदला मँ राष्ट्रीय संकट के समय मँ नेतृत्व केरौ एगो व्यापक सवाल बतैलकै ।

नेकपा एमाले पूर्व विधायक ठाकुर गैरे सेहो सर्वदलीय बैसारमे प्रधानमन्त्री आ गृहमन्त्रीके अनुपस्थितिके आलोचना करैत सुनसरीमे खुलल संकटके प्रति तात्कालिकता आ संवेदनशीलताके अभावके अनुमान लगाबैत बतौलनि ।

देवांगंज अशांति क॑ सरकार केरऽ निपटारा प॑ राजनीतिक टिप्पणीकारऽ के आलोचना जारी छै, जेकरा म॑ बहुत लोगऽ के तर्क छै कि सब राजनीतिक दल आरू राज्य केरऽ संस्थान क॑ मिल क॑ शांति बहाल करै आरू सामाजिक सौहार्द क॑ बचाबै के काम करना चाहियऽ । एम्हर सरकारी अधिकारी सब के कहनाय छनि जे राज्य के एजेंसी सुरक्षा के कायम राखय, घटना के जांच करय आओर आओर बढ़य के रोकय मे सक्रिय रूप सं लागल रहैत अछि.

title: Govt, Nepal Medical Association reach agreement; Health service resumes - The Rising Nepal

full_article:
Kathmandu, July 29: The government and Nepal Medical Association have reached an agreement today. With the signing of the deal, doctors have withdrawn their ongoing protest programmes.

In protest of the incident of misbehave and assault on doctors and health workers, the Nepal Medical Association (NMA) had shut OPD and other services in health facilities across the country on Tuesday and Wednesday, demanding action against the guilty parties.

To resolve the dispute, the Government of Nepal and the Medical Association reached a five-point agreement today.

After discussions at the Ministry of Health and Food Safety with the representatives of Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, and officials of the Nepal Medical Association, the agreement was signed this afternoon.

In this agreement, the government expressed the commitment to effectively implementing the Health Workers and Health Institutions Protection Act, 2066.

According to this Act, the government will issue necessary guidelines to ensure the protection of health workers, coordinate among relevant ministries for legal action in cases of attacks on health workers or damage to health institutions. Likewise, measures will be taken to ensure the security of health institutions.

Similarly, the agreement also includes preparation of a plan to ensure the security of health institutions, and formation of a task force in collaboration with the Nepal Medical Association to implement the plan, with regular reviews of progress.

The agreement states that the Ministry of Health and Food Safety will form a task force within seven days, including participation from the Medical Association, to make necessary amendments related to health to the Consumer Protection Act 2018, based on the task force report.

The agreement was signed by Dr. Parashar Dhungana, Secretary at the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs; Narayan Prasad Sharma Duwadi, Secretary at the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies; Dr. Bikash Devkota, Secretary at the Ministry of Health and Food Hygiene; and Dr. Badri Rijal, President of the Nepal Medical Association.(RSS)

काठमांडू, 29 जुलाई : सरकार आ नेपाल मेडिकल एसोसिएशन के बीच आइ सहमति भेल अछि। सौदा पर हस्ताक्षर के संग डॉक्टर सब अपन जारी विरोध कार्यक्रम वापस ल लेलक अछि।

चिकित्सक आ स्वास्थ्यकर्मी पर दुर्व्यवहार आ मारपीट के घटना के विरोध मे नेपाल मेडिकल एसोसिएशन (एनएमए) दोषी पक्ष के खिलाफ कार्रवाई के मांग करैत मंगल आ बुधदिन देश भरिक स्वास्थ्य सुविधा मे ओपीडी आ अन्य सेवा बंद क देने छल।

विवादक समाधान लेल नेपाल सरकार आ मेडिकल एसोसिएशन आइ पाँच बुँदे सहमतिमे पहुँचल अछि ।

स्वास्थ्य तथा खाद्य सुरक्षा मन्त्रालयमे कानून, न्याय तथा संसदीय मामिला मन्त्रालय, गृहमन्त्रालय, उद्योग, वाणिज्य तथा आपूर्ति मन्त्रालय, आ नेपाल चिकित्सा संघके अधिकारीसबके प्रतिनिधिसभके साथ परिचर्चा के बाद आइ दुपहरमे सम्झौतामे हस्ताक्षर भेल अछि ।

एहि समझौता मे सरकार स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता आ स्वास्थ्य संस्थान संरक्षण अधिनियम, 2066 कए प्रभावी ढंग स लागू करबाक प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त केलक अछि।

एहि अधिनियम क अनुसार सरकार स्वास्थ्यकर्मी क सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करबा लेल आवश्यक दिशा निर्देश जारी करत, स्वास्थ्यकर्मी पर हमला या स्वास्थ्य संस्थान कए नुकसान पहुंचेबाक मामला मे कानूनी कार्रवाई लेल संबंधित मंत्रालय क बीच समन्वय करत। तहिना स्वास्थ्य संस्थान के सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करय के उपाय कएल जाएत.

तहिना एहि समझौता मे स्वास्थ्य संस्थाक सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करबाक योजना तैयार करब, आ योजना केँ लागू करबाक लेल नेपाल चिकित्सा संघक सहयोग सँ कार्यदल केर गठन, प्रगति केर नियमित समीक्षा सेहो शामिल अछि ।

समझौता म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि स्वास्थ्य आरू खाद्य सुरक्षा मंत्रालय टास्क फोर्स केरऽ रिपोर्ट के आधार प॑ उपभोक्ता संरक्षण अधिनियम २०१८ म॑ स्वास्थ्य स॑ जुड़लऽ आवश्यक संशोधन करै लेली मेडिकल एसोसिएशन केरऽ भागीदारी सहित सात दिन के भीतर एगो टास्क फोर्स के गठन करतै ।

समझौता पर कानून, न्याय एवं संसदीय कार्य मंत्रालय के सचिव डॉ. पराशर ढुंगाना; नारायण प्रसाद शर्मा दुवाडी, उद्योग, वाणिज्य एवं आपूर्ति मंत्रालय के सचिव, प्रो. स्वास्थ्य एवं खाद्य स्वच्छता मंत्रालय के सचिव डॉ. विकास देवकोटा, प्रो. एवं नेपाल चिकित्सा संघ के अध्यक्ष डॉ. बद्री रिजाल।(आरएसएस)

Key takeaways

Agricultural carbon markets can boost farm incomes in Nepal. Carbon credits could create a new revenue stream for smallholder farmers while supporting climate-smart agriculture.

Carbon credits could create a new revenue stream for smallholder farmers while supporting climate-smart agriculture. Methane reduction offers major potential. Improved rice and livestock practices could cut emissions and generate significant carbon credit revenues.

Improved rice and livestock practices could cut emissions and generate significant carbon credit revenues. Success depends on strong institutions. Better monitoring, fair benefit-sharing, and cooperative-based farmer participation are essential for scaling agricultural carbon trading.

Climate finance has evolved from a peripheral concern of development policy into a central component of the global financial architecture. Carbon markets allow businesses and other organizations to monetize emissions reductions through credits sold on international exchanges.

Agriculture currently represents only a tiny slice of this activity. The agricultural carbon credit market was valued at just $36.1 million in 2024 out of more than $100 billion globally.

This current landscape—a large compliance market (where governments require regulated entities to pay for emissions, valued at $107 billion in 2025), a small voluntary segment (where companies purchase credits to meet self-determined commitments, valued at just $1.7 billion as of 2024), and within the latter, a near-nonexistent agricultural niche—represents a significant opportunity for agricultural finance. Even a modest reallocation of voluntary credits toward agriculture would represent a large proportional gain for a sector starting from near zero. That, in turn, can provide an important funding stream to drive food system transformation.

Nepal offers a case study for the potential of carbon credits as a means of climate-friendly agricultural finance. The challenges are significant. Key among them will be integrating smallholder farmers into carbon markets. In Nepal, as in other countries, smallholder farmers are almost entirely absent from carbon markets historically dominated by energy corporations and reforestation programs.

Yet expanding smallholder participation (amid a broader market expansion of agriculture) would yield many advantages. Agricultural mitigation, particularly of methane, a potent greenhouse gas (GHG), offers credit buyers measurable, near-term climate benefits; for farming households, carbon markets represent an untapped revenue stream that complements existing activities. They monetize climate-smart farming practices, providing farmers with recurring income that supplements, rather than replaces, existing agricultural earnings. This effort faces some serious obstacles, including integrating smallholders into the carbon market system and distributing benefits equitably.

Nepal’s current carbon market: status, scale, and participants

Nepal contributes only 0.1% of global GHG emissions, yet its community-managed forests, hydropower sector, and agricultural potential make it a credible candidate for carbon market participation.

The Carbon Trading Regulation, 2082, enacted in December 2025 under the Environment Protection Act 2076, established Nepal’s first legal framework for creating, registering, and trading carbon credits, covering forestry, agriculture, hydropower, clean cooking, transport, and waste management.

Until now, Nepal’s carbon market activity has predominantly been restricted to the REDD+ forestry program. Under REDD+, in 2025-2026, it secured a $9.4 million results-based carbon payment from the World Bank and a $55 million purchase agreement with the LEAF Coalition, a public-private initiative that finances the protection of forests. It is the first Asian country to join LEAF. But, as elsewhere, agriculture remains virtually absent from Nepal’s carbon market.

Why agriculture, and why now

Nepali agriculture is often described in terms of decline: falling productivity, shrinking labor availability, and rising import dependency. Agricultural carbon trading offers a pathway to improve those conditions while addressing climate change.

Expanding carbon market access to agriculture matters for two reasons: reducing emissions and generating income. Methane accounts for nearly 50% (28.1 MtCO₂e) of the national GHG profile (59 MtCO₂e), with livestock and crops contributing 18 MtCO₂e and 4.4 MtCO₂e, respectively. These emissions respond to on-farm practice rather than capital-intensive infrastructure and thus do not require large fiscal commitments; alternate wetting and drying (AWD), improved feed formulation, and efficient fertilizer use are established pathways that lower both costs and emissions.

Figure 1

Rice, methane, and alternate wetting and drying

Conventional flooded paddy cultivation is a significant source of methane. AWD involving periodic drainage rather than continuous flooding offers a well-established alternative. A recent meta-analysis found AWD reduces methane emissions by 51.6% compared with continuous flooding; another study in Nepal showed that AWD lowered the volume of water required for irrigation by approximately 57%, often with maintained or increased yields.

AWD requires no major capital investment and is scalable across Nepal’s 1.43 million hectares of rice cultivation, of which about 770,000 hectares (54.5%) are irrigated and potentially amenable to the practice. Available evidence indicates a mitigation potential of roughly 1.2 tCO₂e per hectare annually under AWD. At full scale across 770,000 irrigated hectares, this could generate around 924,000 tCO₂e in annual verified reductions, translating to $12 million-$25 million per year in credit revenue.

AWD should be understood as illustrative rather than a standalone business case. Its value lies in direct agronomic benefits that may matter more to farmers than the carbon payment itself and in demonstrating the type of practice change agricultural carbon finance could reward at scale.

Livestock, methane, and the larger opportunity

Livestock is Nepal’s leading source of agricultural methane, yet its carbon potential receives little attention compared to that of rice. But it warrants treatment on par with rice in any serious assessment of the country’s agricultural carbon opportunity.

Nepal has 5.2 million cattle, 3.3 million buffaloes, and 15.3 million goats, a herd whose scale suggests an opportunity for climate finance that may nationally exceed what rice cultivation can offer. Most livestock emissions arise from enteric fermentation, with manure management contributing a smaller share. Mitigation practices include improved feed formulation and additives such as nitrate or tannin supplements.

Using IPCC Tier 1 emission factors of 1.0 to 1.3 tCO₂e per animal annually, a 10%-15% reduction across half of the national herd could generate $15 million-$30 million per year at current market prices—comparable to, and potentially exceeding, AWD’s estimated returns. Methane’s short atmospheric lifetime makes near-term reductions attractive to buyers, and livestock mitigation maps well onto Nepal’s dairy cooperative infrastructure, allowing faster scaling than AWD.

A broader portfolio: improved livestock, agroforestry and on-farm energy

A durable carbon market strategy for Nepali agriculture should incorporate a portfolio of practices aligned with three revenue streams: production revenue, environmental service payments compensating farmers for stewardship of land and carbon stock, and renewable energy income.

Improved livestock feed and manure management can generate additional credits. Agroforestry and soil carbon practices, such as reduced tillage and biochar application, can sequester carbon while improving soil fertility. On-farm solar for irrigation offers cost savings that complement carbon payments.

For the purposes of carbon markets, each technology carries its own measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) requirements and should not be oversold as an immediate solution. A diversified portfolio, anchored by AWD’s demonstrated feasibility and scaled through cooperative aggregation, offers a more credible path to revenue commensurate with institutional costs.

Building an agricultural carbon trading system

Creating robust agricultural carbon trading will require assembling the necessary institutional architecture.

Figure 2

Measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV)

MRV systems present perhaps the most immediate challenge. Nepal currently lacks agricultural MRV infrastructure capable of large-scale verification. Buyers require assurance that emissions reductions are real, measurable, additional, and permanent, but variability in land size and cropping conditions complicates measurement and imposes costs smallholders cannot bear.

Registries and safeguards against double counting

Transparent accounting systems are essential to prevent double counting, i.e., whether a reduction is sold multiple times or counted toward both national commitments and private offset claims. International scrutiny has intensified, and weak registries risk undermining Nepal’s credibility.

Constitutional and fiscal clarity

A more fundamental issue concerns constitutional authority. The 2025 regulation raises unresolved questions about the allocation of fiscal and natural resource powers under Nepal’s federal constitution, particularly Articles 60 and 116, which govern revenue-sharing across government levels.

This ambiguity is more than a technical concern, since investors and carbon buyers prioritize policy certainty, and unresolved jurisdictional disputes can discourage participation. Legislative amendments clarifying ownership rights and intergovernmental roles would enhance predictability.

Benefit sharing and equity

An equally important question is whether the benefits of carbon credits will reach smallholders who make the effort to participate. In many cases, local producers have received disproportionately small shares of revenue relative to intermediaries.

A prime example is the Kariba REDD+ forest conservation project in Zimbabwe. Launched in 2011, the project was designed to prevent deforestation across 758,000 hectares of land and directly financially support the local communities. The project generated over $100 million in carbon credit sales, but local communities and regional councils doing the ground-level conservation work received a mere $16 million.

Nepal’s program design should adopt a defined benefit-sharing model rather than relying on ad hoc negotiation between farmers and credit buyers. This approach guarantees a fixed farmer share, cooperative dividends channel payment through existing networks, and upfront payment reduces farmers’ cash-flow risk by disbursing revenue before verification.

Source : Authors. Preferred by Nature (Plan Vivo, a community-focused voluntary carbon standard established in 1994, and Acorn, a Rabobank-Microsoft agroforestry program certified by Plan Vivo that returns roughly 70– of revenue to smallholder farmers); Climate Policy Initiative: a cluster-based biochar carbon removal model (Circkular AgroFintech) that pays 60% of revenue upfront to smallholders, with an early-reported 8–10 % income uplift.

Cooperatives as carbon aggregators: a Nepal-specific model

Nepal’s agricultural system is overwhelmingly dominated by smallholders, whose fragmented landholdings make individualized participation prohibitively costly. A scalable aggregation mechanism is therefore indispensable.

Nepal already possesses an underutilized asset for this role: its network of more than 34,000 registered agricultural cooperatives, many deeply embedded in rural communities, positioning them to intermediate between farmers and carbon markets.

Under a cooperative-as-aggregator model, cooperatives would coordinate farmer enrollment, training, data collection, and revenue distribution, bundling emissions reductions across many households into tradable assets and lowering transaction costs.

Cooperatives’ local trust makes farmers more likely to adopt unfamiliar practices such as AWD, and their governance provides a foundation for accountable benefit-sharing.

Building such a system will take time. Not all cooperatives possess the managerial capacity or transparency required, and governance weaknesses remain documented concerns. A successful model would require accreditation, technical support, and independent oversight.

Conclusion: Reframing Nepal’s agricultural future

Carbon markets will not independently transform Nepal’s economy, eliminate its dependency on food imports, or reverse labor migration out of agriculture. Yet agricultural carbon trading can function as a catalytic instrument within a broader agenda of rural revitalization, fiscal resilience, and food system transformation.

Carbon finance also differs structurally from the grants, loans, and remittances on which Nepal has long relied for rural development, reflecting surplus labor and low returns that have driven much of the rural workforce abroad. Because carbon payments are performance-based, they could help retain labor in agriculture.

If the MRV, registry, and benefit-sharing institutions described above are built, the cooperative network is mobilized for aggregation, and farmers employ a diversified portfolio of practices, Nepal’s carbon dividend could extend well beyond emissions reductions. The challenge now is to build institutions capable of capitalizing on this opportunity rather than to merely demonstrate its existence.

प्रमुख टेकअवे

कृषि कार्बन बाजार नेपाल मे खेतक आय बढ़ा सकैत अछि। कार्बन क्रेडिट छोट किसानक कें लेल एकटा नव राजस्व धारा पैदा कयर सकय छै आ जलवायु स्मार्ट कृषि कें समर्थन करय सकय छै.

कार्बन क्रेडिट छोट किसानक कें लेल एकटा नव राजस्व धारा पैदा कयर सकय छै आ जलवायु स्मार्ट कृषि कें समर्थन करय सकय छै. मीथेन मे कमी प्रमुख संभावना प्रदान करैत अछि। चावल आ पशुधन कें बेहतर तरीका सं उत्सर्जन मे कटौती भ सकय छै आ कार्बन क्रेडिट सं काफी राजस्व पैदा भ सकय छै.

चावल आ पशुधन कें बेहतर तरीका सं उत्सर्जन मे कटौती भ सकय छै आ कार्बन क्रेडिट सं काफी राजस्व पैदा भ सकय छै. सफलता मजबूत संस्था पर निर्भर करैत अछि। कृषि कार्बन व्यापार कें स्केल करय कें लेल बेहतर निगरानी, ​​उचित लाभ-बंटवारा, आ सहकारी आधारित किसानक कें भागीदारी आवश्यक छै.

जलवायु वित्त विकास नीति केरऽ परिधीय चिंता स॑ वैश्विक वित्तीय वास्तुकला केरऽ केंद्रीय घटक म॑ बदली गेलऽ छै । कार्बन बाजार व्यवसाय आ अन्य संगठनक कें अंतरराष्ट्रीय एक्सचेंज पर बेचल गेल क्रेडिट कें माध्यम सं उत्सर्जन मे कमी कें मुद्रा बनावा कें अनुमति देयत छै.

कृषि वर्तमान मे एहि गतिविधि क एकटा छोट सन टुकड़ा मात्र क प्रतिनिधित्व करैत अछि । कृषि कार्बन ऋण बाजार केरऽ कीमत 2024 म॑ वैश्विक स्तर प॑ 100 अरब डॉलर स॑ भी अधिक म॑ स॑ महज 36.1 मिलियन डॉलर छेलै ।

इ वर्तमान परिदृश्य-एकटा पैघ अनुपालन बाजार (जतय सरकारक कें द्वारा विनियमित संस्थाक कें उत्सर्जन कें लेल भुगतान करय कें आवश्यकता होयत छै, जेकर मूल्य 2025 मे 107 अरब डॉलर छै), एकटा छोट स्वैच्छिक खंड (जतय कंपनीक स्व-निर्धारित प्रतिबद्धताक कें पूरा करय कें लेल क्रेडिट खरीदय छै, जेकर मूल्य 2024 कें अनुसार महज 1.7 अरब डॉलर छै), आ बाद वाला कें भीतर, लगभग गैर-मौजूद कृषि आला-एकटा महत्वपूर्ण अवसर कें प्रतिनिधित्व करय छै कृषि वित्त। कृषि कें तरफ स्वैच्छिक ऋण कें मामूली पुनर्वितरण सेहो शून्य कें पास सं शुरू होएय वाला क्षेत्र कें लेल एकटा पैघ आनुपातिक लाभ कें प्रतिनिधित्व करतय. जे बदला मे खाद्य प्रणाली परिवर्तन कें बढ़ावा देवय कें लेल एकटा महत्वपूर्ण फंडिंग स्ट्रीम प्रदान कयर सकय छै.

नेपाल जलवायु अनुकूल कृषि वित्त के साधन के रूप में कार्बन क्रेडिट के संभावना के लेल केस स्टडी प्रदान करैत अछि | चुनौती महत्वपूर्ण अछि। एहि मे प्रमुख छोट किसान कए कार्बन बाजार मे शामिल करब होएत। नेपाल म॑ भी अन्य देशऽ के तरह ऐतिहासिक रूप स॑ ऊर्जा निगम आरू पुनर्वनीकरण कार्यक्रमऽ के बोलबाला वाला कार्बन बाजारऽ स॑ लघु किसान लगभग पूरा तरह स॑ अनुपस्थित छै ।

तइयो लघु किसानक कें भागीदारी कें विस्तार सं (कृषि कें व्यापक बाजार विस्तार कें बीच) बहुत फायदा होयत. कृषि शमन, विशेष रूप सं मीथेन, एकटा शक्तिशाली ग्रीनहाउस गैस (जीएचजी) कें, ऋण खरीदारक कें मापल जा सकय वाला, निकट भविष्य कें जलवायु लाभ प्रदान करयत छै; खेती करय वाला घरक कें लेल कार्बन बाजार एकटा अप्रयुक्त राजस्व धारा कें प्रतिनिधित्व करय छै जे मौजूदा गतिविधियक कें पूरक छै. इ जलवायु-स्मार्ट खेती प्रथाक कें मुद्रीकरण करयत छै, जे किसानक कें आवर्ती आय प्रदान करयत छै जे मौजूदा कृषि कमाई कें जगह नहि बल्कि पूरक छै. इ प्रयास कें सामने किच्छू गंभीर बाधाक कें सामना करय पड़य छै, जइ मे लघु किसानक कें कार्बन बाजार प्रणाली मे शामिल करनाय आ लाभ कें समान रूप सं वितरित करनाय शामिल छै.

नेपालक वर्तमान कार्बन बाजार : स्थिति, पैमाना, आ प्रतिभागी |

नेपाल वैश्विक जीएचजी उत्सर्जन मे मात्र 0.1% योगदान दैत अछि, तइयो एकर समुदाय द्वारा प्रबंधित वन, जलविद्युत क्षेत्र, आ कृषि क्षमता एकरा कार्बन बाजार मे भागीदारी लेल विश्वसनीय उम्मीदवार बना दैत अछि ।

पर्यावरण संरक्षण अधिनियम 2076 कें तहत दिसंबर 2025 मे बनल कार्बन व्यापार नियमावली, 2082 मे कार्बन क्रेडिट कें निर्माण, पंजीकरण, आ व्यापार कें लेल नेपाल कें पहिल कानूनी रूपरेखा स्थापित कैल गेलय, जेकरा मे वानिकी, कृषि, जलविद्युत, स्वच्छ खाना बनावा, परिवहन, आ अपशिष्ट प्रबंधन शामिल छै.

एखन धरि नेपाल के कार्बन बाजार गतिविधि मुख्य रूप सं रेड+ वानिकी कार्यक्रम तक सीमित रहल अछि. रेड+ कें तहत, 2025-2026 मे, ओकरा विश्व बैंक सं 9.4 मिलियन डॉलर कें परिणाम आधारित कार्बन भुगतान आ लीफ गठबंधन कें साथ 55 मिलियन डॉलर कें खरीद समझौता सुरक्षित करलकय, जे एकटा सार्वजनिक-निजी पहल छै जे जंगलक कें सुरक्षा कें वित्तपोषण करय छै. ई एशिया केरऽ पहिलऽ देश छेकै जे लीफ म॑ शामिल होय गेलऽ छै । लेकिन, अन्यत्रऽ के तरह, नेपाल केरऽ कार्बन बाजार म॑ कृषि लगभग अनुपस्थित छै ।

खेती किएक, आ आब किएक

नेपाली कृषि के प्रायः गिरावट के संदर्भ में वर्णित करलऽ जाय छै : उत्पादकता में गिरावट, श्रम के उपलब्धता में सिकुड़ना, आरू बढ़तऽ आयात पर निर्भरता । कृषि कार्बन व्यापार जलवायु परिवर्तन कें संबोधित करयत ओय परिस्थितिक मे सुधार कें लेल एकटा मार्ग प्रदान करयत छै.

कृषि कें लेल कार्बन बाजार पहुंच कें विस्तार दू कारण सं मायने रखयत छै: उत्सर्जन मे कमी आ आय पैदा करनाय. राष्ट्रीय जीएचजी प्रोफाइल (59 एमटीसीओ2) कें लगभग 50% (28.1 एमटीसीओ2) मीथेन कें हिस्सा छै, जइ मे पशुधन आ फसलक कें योगदान क्रमशः 18 एमटीसीओ2 आ 4.4 एमटीसीओ2 छै. इ उत्सर्जन पूंजी-गहन बुनियादी ढाँचा कें बजाय खेत पर अभ्यास कें प्रतिक्रिया देयत छै आ अइ प्रकार पैघ राजकोषीय प्रतिबद्धताक कें आवश्यकता नहि होयत छै; वैकल्पिक गीला करनाय आ सुखायनाय (एडब्ल्यूडी), बेहतर चारा कें निर्माण, आ कुशल खाद कें उपयोग स्थापित मार्ग छै जे लागत आ उत्सर्जन दूनू कें कम करएयत छै.

चित्र 1

चावल, मीथेन, आ बारी-बारी स गीला आ सुखायब

पारंपरिक बाढ़ि मे धानक खेती मीथेन केर एकटा महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत अछि । लगातार बाढ़ कें बजाय आवधिक जल निकासी कें शामिल करय वाला एडब्ल्यूडी एकटा सुस्थापित विकल्प प्रदान करयत छै. हाल केरऽ एगो मेटा-एनालिसिस म॑ पता चललै कि एडब्ल्यूडी लगातार बाढ़ के तुलना म॑ मीथेन उत्सर्जन म॑ ५१.६% के कमी करै छै; नेपाल मे एकटा आओर अध्ययन सं पता चलल जे एडब्ल्यूडी सिंचाई के लेल आवश्यक पानिक मात्रा मे लगभग 57% कम केलक, जाहि मे प्रायः पैदावार बनल रहल या बढ़ल.

एडब्ल्यूडी कें कोनों पैघ पूंजी निवेश कें आवश्यकता नहि छै आ इ नेपाल कें 14.3 लाख हेक्टेयर धान खेती मे स्केल करय योग्य छै, जइ मे सं लगभग 770,000 हेक्टेयर (54.5%) सिंचित छै आ संभावित रूप सं प्रथा कें अनुकूल छै. उपलब्ध सबूत एडब्ल्यूडी कें तहत सालाना लगभग 1.2 tCO2e प्रति हेक्टेयर कें शमन क्षमता कें संकेत करयत छै. 770,000 सिंचित हेक्टेयर मे पूरा पैमाना पर, इ सालाना सत्यापित कमी मे लगभग 924,000 टीसीओ2 पैदा कयर सकय छै, जेकर अनुवाद 12 मिलियन-25 मिलियन डॉलर प्रति वर्ष ऋण राजस्व मे होयत छै.

एडब्ल्यूडी कें स्टैंडअलोन बिजनेस केस कें बजाय दृष्टांतात्मक कें रूप मे समझल जेबाक चाही. एकर मूल्य प्रत्यक्ष कृषि लाभ मे निहित छै जे किसानक कें लेल स्वयं कार्बन भुगतान सं बेसि मायने रखय सकय छै आ कृषि कार्बन वित्त पैमाना पर पुरस्कृत कयर सकय वाला अभ्यास परिवर्तन कें प्रकार कें प्रदर्शन करय मे.

पशुधन, मीथेन, आ पैघ अवसर

पशुधन नेपाल केरऽ कृषि मीथेन केरऽ प्रमुख स्रोत छै, तभियो एकरऽ कार्बन क्षमता क॑ चावल के तुलना म॑ बहुत कम ध्यान देलऽ जाय छै । लेकिन देश केरऽ कृषि कार्बन अवसर केरऽ कोनो भी गंभीर आकलन म॑ चावल के बराबर व्यवहार के जरूरत छै ।

नेपाल मे 52 लाख मवेशी, 33 लाख भैंस, आ 1.53 लाख बकरी अछि, जेकर पैमाना जलवायु वित्त के अवसर के सुझाव दैत अछि जे राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर धान के खेती सं बेसी भ सकैत अछि. अधिकतर पशुधन उत्सर्जन आंत कें किण्वन सं होयत छै, जइ मे खाद प्रबंधन कें योगदान कम छै. शमन प्रथाक मे चारा कें बेहतर फॉर्मूलेशन आ एडिटिव्स जैना नाइट्रेट या टैनिन कें पूरक शामिल छै.

आईपीसीसी टीयर 1 उत्सर्जन कारक कें उपयोग करयत 1.0 सं 1.3 tCO2e प्रति जानवर सालाना, राष्ट्रीय झुंड कें आधा मे 10%-15% कें कमी वर्तमान बाजार मूल्यक पर 15 मिलियन-30 मिलियन डॉलर प्रति वर्ष पैदा कयर सकय छै-जेकर तुलना एडब्ल्यूडी कें अनुमानित रिटर्न सं कैल जा सकय छै, आ संभावित रूप सं ओय सं बेसि छै. मीथेन केरऽ छोटऽ वायुमंडलीय जीवनकाल खरीदारऽ लेली निकट भविष्य केरऽ कमी क॑ आकर्षक बनाबै छै, आरू पशुधन शमन नेपाल केरऽ डेयरी सहकारी बुनियादी ढाँचा प॑ अच्छा तरह स॑ नक्शा बनाबै छै, जेकरा स॑ एडब्ल्यूडी स॑ तेज स्केलिंग के अनुमति मिलै छै ।

एकटा व्यापक पोर्टफोलियो: बेहतर पशुधन, कृषि वानिकी आ खेत पर ऊर्जा

नेपाली कृषि कें लेल टिकाऊ कार्बन बाजार रणनीति मे तीन राजस्व धारा कें साथ संरेखित प्रथाक कें पोर्टफोलियो शामिल होबाक चाही: उत्पादन राजस्व, भूमि आ कार्बन स्टॉक कें संचालन कें लेल किसानक कें मुआवजा देवय वाला पर्यावरण सेवा भुगतान, आ अक्षय ऊर्जा आय.

पशुधन कें चारा आ खाद प्रबंधन मे सुधार सं अतिरिक्त क्रेडिट पैदा भ सकय छै. कृषि वानिकी आ मिट्टी कें कार्बन प्रथाक, जेना खेती आ बायोचर कें उपयोग मे कमी, कार्बन कें अलग कयर सकय छै आ मिट्टी कें उर्वरता मे सुधार कयर सकय छै. सिंचाई कें लेल खेत पर सौर ऊर्जा सं लागत मे बचत होयत छै जे कार्बन भुगतान कें पूरक छै.

कार्बन बाजारक कें उद्देश्यक कें लेल, प्रत्येक तकनीक अपन मापन, रिपोर्टिंग, आ सत्यापन (एमआरवी) आवश्यकताक कें वाहक छै आ तत्काल समाधान कें रूप मे बेसि बिक्री नहि कैल जेबाक चाही. एकटा विविध पोर्टफोलियो, जे एडब्ल्यूडी कें प्रदर्शित व्यवहार्यता सं लंगर डालल गेल छै आ सहकारी एकत्रीकरण कें माध्यम सं स्केल कैल गेल छै, संस्थागत लागत कें अनुपात मे राजस्व कें लेल एकटा बेसि विश्वसनीय मार्ग प्रदान करयत छै.

कृषि कार्बन व्यापार प्रणाली के निर्माण

मजबूत कृषि कार्बन व्यापार पैदा करय कें लेल आवश्यक संस्थागत वास्तुकला कें इकट्ठा करय कें आवश्यकता होयत.

चित्र 2

मापन, रिपोर्टिंग, आ सत्यापन (एमआरवी) 1.1.

एमआरवी सिस्टम शायद सबस तत्काल चुनौती पेश करैत अछि। नेपाल मे एखन पैघ पैमाना पर सत्यापन करबा मे सक्षम कृषि एमआरवी बुनियादी ढांचा क अभाव अछि। खरीदारक कें आश्वासन कें आवश्यकता छै की उत्सर्जन मे कमी वास्तविक, मापनीय, अतिरिक्त आ स्थायी छै, मुदा जमीन कें आकार आ फसल कें स्थिति मे परिवर्तनशीलता मापन कें जटिल बनायत छै आ लागत थोपयत छै जे लघु किसानक कें सहन नहि कयर सकय छै.

दोगुना गिनती कें खिलाफ रजिस्ट्री आ सुरक्षा उपाय

पारदर्शी लेखा प्रणाली दोहरा गिनती कें रोकय कें लेल आवश्यक छै, यानी की कोनों कमी कें कई बेर बेचल जाय या राष्ट्रीय प्रतिबद्धता आ निजी ऑफसेट दावा दूनू कें तरफ गिनल जाय. अंतर्राष्ट्रीय जांच तेज भ गेल अछि, आ कमजोर रजिस्ट्री नेपाल के विश्वसनीयता के कमजोर करय के खतरा अछि.

संवैधानिक एवं राजकोषीय स्पष्टता

एकटा बेसी मौलिक मुद्दा संवैधानिक अधिकार स संबंधित अछि। 2025 केरऽ नियमावली म॑ नेपाल केरऽ संघीय संविधान खास करी क॑ अनुच्छेद ६० आरू ११६ के तहत राजकोषीय आरू प्राकृतिक संसाधन शक्ति के आवंटन के बारे म॑ अनसुलझल सवाल उठैलऽ गेलऽ छै, जे सरकारी स्तर प॑ राजस्व के बंटवारा क॑ नियंत्रित करै छै ।

ई अस्पष्टता तकनीकी चिंता स॑ भी अधिक छै, कैन्हेंकि निवेशक आरू कार्बन खरीदार नीतिगत निश्चितता क॑ प्राथमिकता दै छै, आरू अनसुलझे न्यायिक विवाद भागीदारी क॑ हतोत्साहित करी सकै छै । स्वामित्व अधिकार आ अंतरसरकारी भूमिका कें स्पष्ट करय वाला विधायी संशोधन सं पूर्वानुमान मे वृद्धि होयत.

लाभ साझा करब आ इक्विटी

एकटा ओतबे महत्वपूर्ण सवाल इ छै की कार्बन क्रेडिट कें लाभ ओय छोट किसानक तइक पहुंचतय जे भाग लेवा कें प्रयास करय छै. बहुत मामला मे स्थानीय उत्पादक कें मध्यस्थक कें सापेक्ष राजस्व कें अनुपातहीन रूप सं कम हिस्सा भेटल छै.

एकरऽ प्रमुख उदाहरण जिम्बाब्वे म॑ करीबा रेड+ वन संरक्षण परियोजना छै । 2011 मे शुरू कैल गेल इ परियोजना कें डिजाइन 758,000 हेक्टेयर जमीन मे जंगलक कें कटाई कें रोकय आ स्थानीय समुदायक कें सीधा आर्थिक सहायता कें लेल बनायल गेलय छेलै. एहि परियोजना स कार्बन क्रेडिट बिक्री 10 करोड़ डॉलर स बेसी भेल, मुदा जमीनी स्तर पर संरक्षण क काज करय वाला स्थानीय समुदाय आ क्षेत्रीय परिषद कए महज 1.6 करोड़ डॉलर भेटल।

नेपाल केरऽ कार्यक्रम डिजाइन म॑ किसान आरू ऋण खरीदारऽ के बीच तदर्थ वार्ता प॑ भरोसा नै करी क॑ परिभाषित लाभ-साझेदारी मॉडल अपनाना चाहियऽ । इ दृष्टिकोण एकटा निश्चित किसान हिस्सेदारी कें गारंटी देयत छै, सहकारी लाभांश मौजूदा नेटवर्क कें माध्यम सं भुगतान चैनल करयत छै, आ अपफ्रंट भुगतान सत्यापन सं पहिले राजस्व कें वितरण करयत किसानक कें नकदी-प्रवाह कें जोखिम कें कम करयत छै.

चित्र 3

नोट: प्रत्येक सड़क किसानक कें कार्बन क्रेडिट राजस्व कें वितरण कें लेल एकटा अलग तंत्र कें प्रतिनिधित्व करयत छै; मॉडल परस्पर विरोधी नहि अछि।

साभार : लेखक। प्रकृति कें द्वारा पसंदीदा (प्लान विवो, 1994 मे स्थापित एकटा समुदाय-केंद्रित स्वैच्छिक कार्बन मानक, आ एकॉर्न, प्लान विवो दूवारा प्रमाणित एकटा राबोबैंक-माइक्रोसॉफ्ट कृषि वानिकी कार्यक्रम जे लघु किसानक कें लगभग 70– राजस्व वापस करयत छै); जलवायु नीति पहल: एकटा क्लस्टर आधारित बायोचर कार्बन हटावय कें मॉडल (सर्कुलर एग्रोफिनटेक) जे लघु किसानक कें 60% राजस्व कें अग्रिम भुगतान करयत छै, जइ मे शुरु आती रिपोर्ट कैल गेल 8-10 % आय मे वृद्धि होयत छै.

कार्बन एग्रीगेटर के रूप में सहकारी : एक नेपाल-विशिष्ट मॉडल |

नेपाल केरऽ कृषि व्यवस्था म॑ लघु किसानऽ के भारी बोलबाला छै, जेकरऽ खंडित जमीन के कारण व्यक्तिगत भागीदारी निषेधात्मक रूप स॑ महँग होय जाय छै । अतः एकटा स्केल करय योग्य एकत्रीकरण तंत्र अनिवार्य अछि ।

नेपाल कें पास पहिने सं अइ भूमिका कें लेल एकटा कम उपयोग कैल गेल संपत्ति छै: ओकर 34,000 सं बेसि पंजीकृत कृषि सहकारी समितियक कें नेटवर्क, जे बहुत सं ग्रामीण समुदायक मे गहराई सं समाहित छै, जे किसान आ कार्बन बाजारक कें बीच मध्यवर्ती कें स्थिति मे छै.

सहकारी-एज-एग्रीगेटर मॉडल कें तहत सहकारी किसानक कें नामांकन, प्रशिक्षण, आंकड़ा संग्रहण, आ राजस्व वितरण कें समन्वय करतय, जे बहुत सं घरक मे उत्सर्जन मे कमी कें व्यापारिक संपत्तियक मे बंडल करतय आ लेनदेन लागत मे कमी करतय.

सहकारी संस्थाक कें स्थानीय विश्वास किसानक कें एडब्ल्यूडी जैना अपरिचित प्रथाक कें अपनावय कें संभावना बेसि बनायत छै, आ ओकर शासन जवाबदेह लाभ-साझेदारी कें लेल आधार प्रदान करयत छै.

एहन व्यवस्था बनेबा मे समय लागत। सब सहकारी कें पास आवश्यक प्रबंधकीय क्षमता या पारदर्शिता नहि छै, आ शासन कमजोरी दस्तावेजबद्ध चिंता बनल छै. एकटा सफल मॉडल कें लेल मान्यता, तकनीकी सहायता, आ स्वतंत्र निगरानी कें आवश्यकता होयत.

निष्कर्ष : नेपाल के कृषि भविष्य के पुनः रूपरेखा बनाना |

कार्बन बाजार नेपाल केरऽ अर्थव्यवस्था म॑ स्वतंत्र रूप स॑ बदलाव नै आबै वाला छै, खाद्य आयात प॑ ओकरऽ निर्भरता खतम नै होतै, नै ही खेती स॑ बाहर मजदूरऽ के पलायन क॑ उलटैलऽ जैतै । तइयो कृषि कार्बन व्यापार ग्रामीण पुनर्जीवन, राजकोषीय लचीलापन, आ खाद्य प्रणाली परिवर्तन कें एकटा व्यापक एजेंडा कें भीतर एकटा उत्प्रेरक उपकरण कें रूप मे काज कयर सकय छै.

कार्बन वित्त संरचनात्मक रूप स॑ भी अनुदान, ऋण, आरू रेमिटंस स॑ भिन्न छै, जेकरा प॑ नेपाल बहुत दिन स॑ ग्रामीण विकास लेली निर्भर छै, जे अधिशेष श्रम आरू कम रिटर्न क॑ दर्शाबै छै जे ग्रामीण कार्यबल केरऽ बहुत हिस्सा क॑ विदेश म॑ प्रेरित करलकै । चूँकि कार्बन भुगतान प्रदर्शन आधारित छै, इ कृषि मे श्रम कें बरकरार रखय मे मदद कयर सकय छै.

यदि ऊपर वर्णित एमआरवी, रजिस्ट्री, आ लाभ साझा करय वाला संस्थाक कें निर्माण कैल जायत छै, सहकारी नेटवर्क कें एकत्रीकरण कें लेल जुटाएल जायत छै, आ किसानक कें प्रथाक कें विविध पोर्टफोलियो कें रोजगार देल जायत छै, त नेपाल कें कार्बन लाभांश उत्सर्जन मे कमी सं काफी आगू बढ़ सकय छै. आब चुनौती ई छै कि खाली एकरऽ अस्तित्व के प्रदर्शन नै करी क॑ ई अवसर के फायदा उठाबै म॑ सक्षम संस्था के निर्माण करलऽ जाय ।

title: Nepal Loses to Netherlands by 57 Runs in ICC CWC League 2 - Ratopati
description: Nepal Loses to Netherlands by 57 Runs in ICC CWC League 2  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal has been defeated by Netherlands by 57 runs in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 match.

Batting first in the match, Netherlands scored 225 runs for the loss of 9 wickets in the stipulated 50 overs. Noah Cross contributed 70 runs off 93 balls for the Netherlands, while Scott Edwards played a half-century innings of 57 runs off 91 balls. Similarly, Logan van Beek added 27 runs off 27 balls.

In bowling, Nepal's Karan KC took 4 wickets for 30 runs in 10 overs. Dipendra Singh Airee gave 30 runs for 2 wickets in 5 overs, and Lalit Rajbanshi took 1 wicket for 32 runs in 10 overs.

The Nepali team, chasing a target of 226 runs, was all out for 168 runs in 48 overs. Asif Sheikh scored a maximum of 38 runs off 78 balls for Nepal. Similarly, Rohit Paudel scored 26 runs off 38 balls and Karan KC scored 23 runs off 29 balls.

To stop Nepal cheaply, Netherlands bowler Kyle Klein took 3 wickets for 26 runs in 8 overs. Logan van Beek took 2 wickets for 16 runs in 6 overs and Jack Lyon-Casett took 2 wickets for 21 runs in 7 overs.

Noah Cross of the Netherlands, who played a crucial innings of 70 runs off 93 balls in the match, was declared the 'Player of the Match'.

title: Nepal's tiger numbers climb 20 percent to estimated 429: Survey - Phys.org
description: Nepal's tiger numbers climb 20 percent to estimated 429: Survey  Phys.org
publisher.title: Phys.org
full_article:
Nepal's tiger population has risen roughly 20 percent in the past four years to an estimated 429, officials said, a conservation milestone despite challenges from human-wildlife conflict.

Nepal's tiger population has risen by roughly 20% in the past four years to an estimated 429, officials said Wednesday, a conservation milestone despite challenges from human-wildlife conflict.

The latest nationwide survey found tiger numbers had increased from 355 in 2022, reinforcing the Himalayan nation's reputation as a success story in big-cat conservation.

"The data analysis shows that the tiger population has increased by 5% each year, and we are happy to see this increasing trend," Bed Kumar Dhakal, spokesman for Nepal's Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, told AFP.

The survey was conducted between December and July and was announced to coincide with International Tiger Day. It covered more than 7,300 square kilometers (2,820 square miles) of Nepal's southern plains that are home to the predators.

Wildlife officials deployed more than 3,600 motion-sensitive cameras across five protected areas, with experts analyzing thousands of images to identify individual tigers by their distinctive stripe patterns.

"The reason behind the increasing number of tigers is because we could keep their habitat secure," said conservation department ecologist Hari Bhadra Acharya.

Deforestation, habitat loss and poaching have been major challenges for tiger populations across Asia, and Nepal has won international praise for reversing the decline.

In 2010, Nepal joined 12 other countries in pledging to double tiger numbers by 2022.

It became the first nation to meet that goal, boosting its tiger population to 355 in 2022 from about 121 in 2009.

Tiger attacks

However, the conservation success has also brought unintended risks for communities living near tiger habitats.

Government data shows at least 38 people were killed in tiger attacks between 2019 and 2023.

"The local communities played a crucial role in increasing the tiger numbers, but the government and organizations are not taking action when the tigers are attacking the same communities," said Nischal Neupane, an advocate for tiger victims in Bardiya district.

The district is home to 112 tigers, up from only 18 in 2009.

WWF Nepal country representative Ghana Shyam Gurung said conservation gains must be matched by efforts to ensure "people and wildlife can thrive together."

"By investing in effective co-existence programs, Nepal can continue to offer a powerful model for other tiger range countries."

More than 100,000 tigers roamed the wild at the start of the 20th century, but global numbers plunged to an estimated 3,200 in 2010 before recovering in parts of Asia through intensified conservation efforts.

नेपाल के बाघ के आबादी पिछला चारि साल में लगभग 20 प्रतिशत बढ़ि क अनुमानित 429 भ गेल अछि, अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, मानव-वन्यजीव संघर्ष के चुनौती के बावजूद संरक्षण के मील के पत्थर अछि।

मानव-वन्यजीव संघर्ष के चुनौती के बावजूद संरक्षण के मील के पत्थर बुधदिन अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, नेपाल के बाघ के आबादी पिछला चारि साल में लगभग 20% बढ़ि क अनुमानित 429 भ गेल अछि।

ताजा देशव्यापी सर्वेक्षण म॑ पता चललै कि बाघऽ के संख्या २०२२ म॑ ३५५ स॑ बढ़ी गेलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ हिमालयी राष्ट्र केरऽ प्रतिष्ठा क॑ मजबूत करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै कि ई बड़ऽ बिल्ली के संरक्षण म॑ सफलता के कहानी छेकै ।

नेपालक राष्ट्रिय उद्यान आ वन्यजीव संरक्षण विभागक प्रवक्ता बेड कुमार ढकाल एएफपी केँ कहलनि जे, आंकड़ा विश्लेषण सँ पता चलैत अछि जे बाघक आबादी मे हरेक वर्ष ५% वृद्धि भेल अछि, आ ई बढ़ैत प्रवृत्ति देखि हमरा सभ केँ खुशी भ’ रहल अछि।

ई सर्वेक्षण दिसंबर आरू जुलाई के बीच करलौ गेलौ छेलै आरू एकरौ घोषणा अंतरराष्ट्रीय बाघ दिवस के साथ मेल खाबै के घोषणा करलौ गेलौ छेलै । ई नेपाल केरऽ दक्षिणी मैदान केरऽ ७,३०० वर्ग किलोमीटर (२,८२० वर्ग मील) स॑ भी अधिक क्षेत्र क॑ कवर करलकै जेकरा म॑ शिकारी जानवरऽ के निवास छै ।

वन्यजीव अधिकारी न॑ पांच संरक्षित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ ३,६०० स॑ भी अधिक गति संवेदनशील कैमरा तैनात करलकै, जेकरा म॑ विशेषज्ञ न॑ हजारों छवि के विश्लेषण करी क॑ अलग-अलग बाघऽ के पहचान ओकरऽ विशिष्ट पट्टी पैटर्न स॑ करलकै ।

संरक्षण विभाग के पारिस्थितिकीविद हरि भद्र आचार्य कहलनि जे, बाघ के बढ़ैत संख्या के पाछु के कारण ई अछि जे हम ओकर आवास सुरक्षित राखि सकैत छलहुं।

पूरा एशिया में बाघ के आबादी के लेल जंगल के कटाई, आवास के नुकसान आ शिकार प्रमुख चुनौती रहल अछि, आ नेपाल एहि गिरावट के उलटय लेल अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रशंसा जीतने अछि.

2010 मे नेपाल 12 अन्य देशक संग 2022 धरि बाघक संख्या दुगुना करबाक वचन देलक।

ई लक्ष्य क॑ पूरा करै वाला पहलऽ राष्ट्र बनलै, जेकरा स॑ ओकरऽ बाघऽ के आबादी २००९ म॑ लगभग १२१ स॑ बढ़ी क॑ २०२२ म॑ ३५५ होय गेलै ।

बाघ हमला करैत अछि

लेकिन संरक्षण केरऽ सफलता स॑ बाघऽ के आवास के पास रह॑ वाला समुदायऽ लेली भी अनचाहा जोखिम पैदा होय गेलऽ छै ।

सरकारी आंकड़ा बताबैत अछि जे 2019 सं 2023 के बीच बाघ हमला मे कम सं कम 38 लोक के मौत भ गेल छल.

बर्दिया जिला के बाघ पीड़ित के पैरवीकार निश्चल नेउपाने कहलनि जे, बाघ के संख्या बढ़ाबय मे स्थानीय समुदाय के अहम भूमिका छल, मुदा सरकार आ संगठन तखन कार्रवाई नहि क रहल अछि जखन बाघ ओही समुदाय पर हमला क रहल अछि।

एहि जिला मे 112 टा बाघ अछि, जे 2009 मे मात्र 18 टा छल।

डब्ल्यूडब्ल्यूएफ नेपाल के देश प्रतिनिधि घाना श्याम गुरुंग कहलनि जे संरक्षण के लाभ के बराबरी ई सुनिश्चित करय के प्रयास सं करय पड़त जे “लोक आ वन्यजीव एक संग पनपि सकय.”

"प्रभावी सह-अस्तित्व कार्यक्रम मँ निवेश करी क नेपाल अन्य टाइगर रेंज देशौ लेली एगो शक्तिशाली मॉडल जारी रखै सकै छै।"

20वीं सदी केरऽ शुरुआत म॑ एक लाख स॑ भी अधिक बाघ जंगल म॑ घूमी रहलऽ छेलै, लेकिन संरक्षण केरऽ तेज प्रयास के माध्यम स॑ एशिया केरऽ कुछ हिस्सा म॑ ठीक होय स॑ पहल॑ २०१० म॑ वैश्विक संख्या म॑ गिरावट आबी क॑ अनुमानित ३,२०० होय गेलै ।

प्रमुख अवधारणा खतरा मे पड़ल प्रजातिवन्यजीवपशु आ पौधा जनगणना गर्जना बिल्ली

title: Muslim vendor assaulted by Hindu mob amid rising religious tensions in Nepal - Muslim Network TV
description: Muslim vendor assaulted by Hindu mob amid rising religious tensions in Nepal  Muslim Network TV
publisher.title: Muslim Network TV
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal (MNTV) — A Muslim ice cream vendor has alleged that he was assaulted by a Hindu extremist mob, forced to chant Hindu religious slogans and robbed of his merchandise in southeastern Nepal, in an incident that has heightened concerns over rising religious intolerance in the Himalayan nation.

According to local media reports, the attack took place in the Kaptanganj area of Sunsari district following recent communal unrest between Hindu and Muslim communities in the region.

The vendor said a group of men intercepted him while he was selling ice cream and demanded that he chant “Jai Shri Ram,” a Hindu religious slogan that has increasingly been used by Hindu extremist groups in South Asia as a political rallying cry.

He alleged that when he refused, the men assaulted him before looting his ice cream and other belongings.

A separate attack targeting another Muslim man was also reported in Inaruwa, the district headquarters of Sunsari.

The victim alleged that members of a group associated with a Hindu organization beat him with sticks while shouting the same slogan and vandalized his motorcycle before fleeing.

The incidents come days after communal tensions flared in parts of Sunsari district over disputes surrounding the playing of loud religious music, the display of religious flags and Hindu religious processions.

The disagreements reportedly escalated into clashes between members of the Hindu and Muslim communities, prompting heightened security in the area.

While Nepal has long been regarded as a religiously diverse society where Hindu, Buddhist and Muslim communities have largely coexisted peacefully, rights advocates have increasingly warned of the growing influence of Hindu extremist groups in recent years.

title: Nepal at a Strategic Crossroads - Khabarhub

full_article:
Nepal stands at a defining strategic moment, the crossroads of history. For more than three decades, the country has experienced repeated political transitions, yet genuine national transformation has remained elusive.

The current administration, armed with an record parliamentary mandate and high public expectations, has perhaps the greatest opportunity since 1990 to change this trajectory. Whether it succeeds will determine if Nepal finally enters an era of strategic stability or once again descends into strategic drift or another cycle of political uncertainty.

Consecutively “National Strategic Confidence”—vital for Nepal—grows directly from political stability, institutional credibility, economic resilience, effective governance, and a shared national vision. Nepal urgently needs this strategic confidence because national credibility policy cannot succeed without strong solidarity and assurance at home.

Ultimately, only a confident nation can pursue an independent, consistent, and resilient national policy, making this domestic trust the foundational bedrock upon which Nepal must build its international engagement.

Nepal’s Democratic Journey: Four Phases of Political Transition

Nepal’s political evolution/transition since the restoration of democracy from 1990 can be understood through four distinct phases: “expectation and aspiration”; “resistance” both geopolitical and structural; “strategic confusion”, and finally, the choice between “strategic breakthrough” for success or “strategic breakdown” with another national crisis.

The Politics of Expectation: Three Decades of Democratic Aspirations

The first period generated extraordinary optimism. The restoration of democracy with the 1990 Constitution establishing a multi-party democracy and constitutional monarchy, King Gyanendra dismisses the government, declares a state of emergency, and assumes absolute power in February 2005, Mainstream political parties (Seven Party Alliance) and Maoist rebels sign a 12-point understanding in Delhi: November 2005, the 2006 Comprehensive Peace Agreement following Janandolan-II, transition to Federal Republic in 2008, the Constitution of 2015, the Gen Z uprising, though not for the first time, the emergence of the current two-thirds government all vowed a new political beginning.

Rather, it serves as a decisive phase that offers the first indication of the direction in which the government intends to lead the country. For this reason, the first hundred days are best understood as an initial test of policy priorities, leadership style, governance, and administrative culture.

Citizens expected accountable governance, economic opportunity, institutional reform, and a state capable of delivering results. Each milestone raised hopes that Nepal had finally found a stable political destination. But in vain presented three constitutions; the 9 November 1990, promulgated by King Birendra, which ended the absolute Panchayat system and introduced a multiparty parliamentary democracy with a constitutional monarch.

The 2007 interim constitution, which brought the warring factions the Maoists into the democratic framework replaced by the second constituent Assembly 2015 constitution embarking as a federal secular republic.

The Dynamics of Strategic Resistance (Political Change Meets Structural Resistance)

Yet every wave of optimism encountered a second phase: “strategic resistance”. Nepal’s transformation has been constrained by both external and internal forces. In Nepal, every political shift carries the seeds of its own immediate resistance, ensuring that no political settlement is ever truly final. These institutional transitions trigger strategic counter-mobilizations by marginalized or rival factions, as seen in the immediate after the declaration of the 2015 constitution instantly triggered intense Madhesi and Tharu resistance and border blockades due to representation grievances.

The frequent coalition shift when swapping or reshuffling the cabinet, the newly displaced parties instantly launch street agitations or parliamentary obstructions.

Geopolitically, the country has had to navigate the competing interests of China, India, and the U.S. led west while preserving its strategic autonomy. Domestically, however, the greater challenge has often been structural rather than political. Entrenched political interests, bureaucratic inertia, weak state institutions, fragmented governance, and deeply embedded patronage networks have repeatedly resisted meaningful reform. Governments changed, constitutions were rewritten, and new political coalitions emerged, but the underlying institutions that citizens depended upon evolved far more slowly.

The Erosion of Public Expectations

This structural resistance has steadily diminished public expectations. Many Nepalis have witnessed successive governments promising prosperity, employment, better public services, and accountable governance, only to encounter the same obstacles: delayed infrastructure projects, politicized public institutions, inconsistent policy implementation, institutional corruption, weak service delivery, and limited accountability for poor performance.

The frequent turnover of governments has often interrupted long-term reforms before they could take root, while the politicization of the bureaucracy has reduced institutional continuity. As a result, reform has become episodic rather than sustained.

The consequence is not merely slower economic development but a gradual erosion of public confidence. When ambitious policies repeatedly fail to translate into visible improvements in daily life, citizens begin lowering their expectations of what the state can realistically deliver.

This helps explain why increasing numbers of young Nepalis seek opportunities abroad, why trust in public institutions remains fragile, and why each new political transition is often met with cautious hope rather than enduring confidence. Changing governments proved easier than changing the system itself; the real challenge has always been transforming the institutions, incentives, and governance culture that shape national outcomes.

The Era of Strategic Confusion

This resistance gave birth to a third phase: “strategic confusion”. Rather than pursuing a coherent national vision, successive governments have largely reacted to immediate political pressures. Foreign policy has often oscillated instead of following a consistent long-term strategy, while domestic politics has prioritized coalition survival over state-building.

Governments increasingly became reactive rather than strategic. Coalition arithmetic replaced long-term national planning. Foreign policy oscillated between competing pressures instead of pursuing a coherent national strategy. State institutions focused on managing crises rather than preventing them. Politics became tactical; governance lost its strategic direction.

Strategic confusion in Nepal’s political transition has unfolded through repeated cycles of hope followed by national crisis. The restoration of democracy in 1990 was soon overshadowed by the Maoist insurgency, which erupted in 1996 against a democratically elected government and ultimately claimed more than 17,000 lives while profoundly weakening state institutions.

The 2006 People’s Movement and the Comprehensive Peace Agreement created another historic opportunity, yet the First Constituent Assembly, elected in 2008 with a strong public mandate to draft a new constitution, was dissolved in 2012 after failing to produce one despite four extensions of its tenure. Even after the Constitution of 2015 established a secular federal democratic republic, expectations of political stability and effective governance remained largely unmet.

Frequent changes of government, coalition instability, inconsistent policy implementation, bureaucratic inertia, politicization of public institutions, weak administrative capacity, corruption, and patronage politics repeatedly prevented governments from translating political change into institutional transformation and improved public services.

As a result, citizens increasingly witnessed governments changing while the governance system itself remained largely unchanged. The lesson from the past three decades is therefore clear: Nepal’s principal challenge has not been a lack of political change but a failure to build capable institutions that can consistently implement reforms, deliver public services, and sustain long-term national development.

It is against this historical backdrop that the new administration is being judged. The public expects not simply another government with a new political mandate, but one capable of breaking the cycle by transforming political commitment into durable institutional reform, effective governance, and measurable improvements in citizens’ lives.

The democratic mandates needed in a national crisis.

The First 100 Days: From Public Mandate to Strategic Direction

Nepal’s new administration has reached a decisive crossroads. Like previous political transitions, this period reflects the convergence of public expectations, organized resistance, and rising strategic confusion.

Marking the completion of its first 100 days and 100 foundational objectives, Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) government led by Prime Minister Balen Shah led new administration now faces its most consequential moment yet: a fragile balancing act between a historic breakthrough and a total breakdown. A decisive crossroads where the government must balance high public expectations against rising public confusion and organized resistance.

The strategic outcome of this high-stakes period will depend on the administration’s ability to convert its aggressive anti-corruption momentum into stable, rules-based institutional governance. If the government manages to successfully navigate the thin line between an institutional breakthrough and a systemic breakdown, it can institutionalize its digital and economic policy reforms, cement long-term stability, and permanently dismantle entrenched political patronage.

Conversely, failing to overcome the overlapping forces of bureaucratic and structural resistance will stall its ambitious roadmap, triggering a breakdown that deepens societal confusion and risks fracturing the administration’s populist.

The first 100 days of any new government are often viewed as an indicator of its early success or failure. From a broader strategic perspective, however, this period is not intended to provide a final assessment of a government’s performance.

Conversely, a failure to defeat the overlapping forces of bureaucratic and structural opposition risks a breakdown, fracturing the government’s populist mandate and stalling Nepal’s national roadmap once again.

Rather, it serves as a decisive phase that offers the first indication of the direction in which the government intends to lead the country. For this reason, the first hundred days are best understood as an initial test of policy priorities, leadership style, governance, and administrative culture.

A Historic Opportunity to Redefine Governance

This is more than a mere change of government. It represents the first real test of an alternative governance culture that citizens have long sought-after decades of political instability, weak governance, institutional corruption, excessive politicization, and bureaucratic inertia. The public did not vote simply for a change of government; they expected a change in the political system and the governance model or the way the country is governed.

The current government possesses political legitimacy, parliamentary strength, and a public mandate that few administrations have enjoyed. These advantages create an opportunity not merely to govern but to redefine governance itself. However, mandates and trust alone do not produce transformation or achievements. They merely create the conditions under which transformation becomes possible only if it can be translated into institutional reform, effective public service delivery, transparency, professionalism, and results-oriented administration.

From Political Management to Strategic Governance

From a strategic perspective, the government’s first few months have demonstrated both promise and warning signs. Political energy has been invested in establishing authority and managing competing expectations, but the country now requires a shift from political management to strategic governance. Citizens are no longer impressed by rhetoric.

They are looking for institutional/administrative reform, economic revival, good governance through better public services, predictable foreign policy, and restored confidence in the state. These pillars will ultimately determine the government’s political credibility over the next five years.

The government has already sent several important signals. Administrative restructuring, the review of ministries, investigations into public assets, expansion of digital public services, a strong public commitment to combating corruption, and decisions challenging long-established administrative practices all indicate that this government does not intend to preserve the status quo.

Nevertheless, the true measure of these initiatives lies not in the policies announced but, in their implementation, institutional impact, and administrative capacity. The challenge is therefore no longer to formulate new policies, but to demonstrate the ability to implement existing commitments effectively. The success of any reform should be measured not by declarations but by tangible institutional outcomes.

The Choice Between Strategic Breakthrough and Strategic Breakdown: Implementation Will Determine Success

History suggests that governments often fail not because they lack political power but because they lack strategic objectives. Nepal has repeatedly mistaken political success for national success. Winning elections, forming governments, or commanding parliamentary majorities are only means; they are not the end. The true measure of success lies in whether institutions become stronger than personalities, policies outlast governments, and national interests prevail over partisan calculations.

The choice before Nepal is therefore straightforward. The government can pursue a strategic agenda that strengthens institutions, restores public trust, modernizes governance, and positions Nepal confidently within an increasingly competitive geopolitical environment. Or it can become another administration consumed by short-term political calculations, leaving the underlying structural problems untouched.

The historic responsibility before Nepal today is to choose coordination over division, confidence over despair, and strategic thinking over reactive politics. If Nepal can effectively leverage its geography, capabilities, and opportunities, strategic success will not remain merely a possibility—it will become a national necessity.

This critical milestone represents a high-stakes crossroads where the state must balance surging public expectations against systemic, organized resistance and deep-seated political confusion. Moving past the historical cycle of rapid, fragile power shifts, the administration’s core challenge is to convert its intense anti-corruption momentum and institutional reform agenda into a lasting rule-based governance model.

If the administration successfully navigates this precarious boundary, it can institutionalize its digital and economic policies, dismantle entrenched patronage networks, and achieve a historic breakthrough. Conversely, a failure to defeat the overlapping forces of bureaucratic and structural opposition risks a breakdown, fracturing the government’s populist mandate and stalling Nepal’s national roadmap once again.

The coming months will determine whether Nepal’s latest political transition becomes the country’s long-awaited crowning achievement or merely another chapter in its recurring cycle of instability. The opportunity is historic. So too is the responsibility.

The question today is not merely about changing a government; it is about transforming the nation. If the necessary transformation does not take place today, the nation may have to pay a profound substancial strategic retribution. Continuously postponing change does not only mean losing opportunities; it risks pushing Nepal’s future into greater volatility, uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity.

However, Nepal’s journey is not merely a story of expectations, resistance, confusion, or crisis; it is also a journey of possibility, confidence, and strategic success. The need of the hour is not to remain trapped in past structural constraints and strategic ambiguity, but to pursue a “Strategic Breakthrough” through a clear national vision, capable institutions, strategic structures, and long-term strategic thinking.

The core objective of Nepal’s national interest is not to move toward fragmentation or decline, but to build “National Strategic Confidence” by bringing together all stakeholders, sectors, and forces of society. Only such confidence can strengthen Nepal’s sovereignty, stability, prosperity, and international standing.

The historic responsibility before Nepal today is to choose coordination over division, confidence over despair, and strategic thinking over reactive politics. If Nepal can effectively leverage its geography, capabilities, and opportunities, strategic success will not remain merely a possibility—it will become a national necessity.
